restaurants.note: Dinner service is 16:00 to 20:00 with last order 19:30. The descent from Kami-Daigo is the part of this day that can run long, and the backup below trades until one in the morning. Reservations are not accepted at all: numbered tickets are issued at the door, and with 21 seats a wait is plausible between 18:00 and 19:00. ⚠ Like Morita-ya eleven floors above it, it follows the department store's own calendar, which is not published far enough ahead to read; tonight's backup is outside that building.

Five minutes on foot from the hotel, and it runs to one in the morning — if Daigo runs past the primary's 19:30 last order, there is no hour tonight can reach at which this kitchen is shut. ⚑ Check the sign on arrival: a second Kyoto shop at Sanjō-Kawaramachi keeps the same Thursday closure at a different address, so the closing day alone will not tell the two apart. This is the honten, at Higashi-Shiokōji Mukaihata-chō 845.

meals.time_hint: In the Nakasenbon cluster, roughly 11:30–12:15 — out of the Zaō-dō and Yoshimizu, before the climb to Kami-senbon

restaurants.note: Sixty-three seats, tables and tatami, which is what makes it walk-in-safe on a peak autumn day; no table can be booked here in any case. ⚠ Its two channels name two different card brands and neither names Visa or Mastercard, so carry cash for it. ⚑ Lunch here is not optional — the mountain eateries close around 16:00 to 17:00, so this is the day's only meal on the ridge. Dinner is back in Kyoto.

Thirty seconds along the frontage from the one above, so checking it costs nothing — and it is the bigger room of the two, 66 seats inside and 6 on a terrace, and it takes cards. ⚠ Its closing days are irregular on both of the channels that carry it and neither publishes a policy, so an open day cannot be assumed. ⚑ Behind both there is a third option, and it is native here rather than a fallback: kakinoha-zushi is packaged, room-temperature, leaf-wrapped food designed to be carried, and Yakko, Tatsumi (たつみ) and Daiyo (醍予) all sell it over the counter — so if every seat in the village is taken on a peak Thursday, buy a box and eat it at the Hanayagura viewpoint on the way up. That is the historically correct version of the day. ⚑ And one named stop that is not lunch: Nakai Shunpū-dō (中井春風堂) at Yoshinoyama 545, also in front of the Zaō-dō. Yoshino-honkuzu kuzumochi and kuzukiri, ¥900 each, made to order in about twenty minutes and with a stated shelf life of ten minutes — which is why the shop is famous. Walk-in is accepted; same-day in-store booking from 09:30 is how the wait is avoided, and the owner works alone so quantities are limited. Its hours and closing days are not published anywhere. Taking it means arriving at Yakko earlier, not later.

meals.time_hint: At base — back at Kyoto Station around 17:30, or 18:15–18:30 on the full version, and it may slip

restaurants.note: Five to eight minutes from the hotel, on the west side of the station. Last order 21:30, which leaves at least three hours in hand for a Yoshino return that may slip. ⚑ Eleven seats and no reservations, and the line has never been counted — but the same three hours that absorb the slip absorb a wait, so if there is one, walk away and come back rather than stand in it. ⚠ It closes on irregular days that it publishes nowhere readable.

On the second basement level at Kyoto Station's east exit — 136 m, no street and no weather, on the night the day is most likely to arrive late and tired. ⚠ Two of its three channels print 07:00 to 22:00 with last order 21:30 and the third prints a wider 06:00 to 23:00 on weekdays. Work to the narrower pair; it is the one two channels agree on.

meals.time_hint: At base — back at Kyoto Station around 17:00–18:00, on the last Kyoto night

restaurants.note: Last order 21:30. ⚠ Closed Wednesdays and on the third Thursday of the month — today is neither. The shop's one channel of its own is an Instagram account, manbo_2020; read it in the fortnight before you fly.

Gojō — one stop on the Karasuma subway, or about thirteen minutes on foot. ⚑ One thing to know before walking over: the evening service does not start until 18:00, so on a day that ends between 17:00 and 18:00 this is a wait-a-little backup rather than an immediate one. Last order 21:30. ⚠ Its sources contradict each other about its closing day, so treat that as unknown.

meals.time_hint: In the station district, 12:05–13:05 — bags into the hotel cloakroom off the 11:38 arrival, Shukkei-en at 13:15

restaurants.note: Ten minutes on foot from the Shinkansen north exit; on this day the queue is inside the station, not out here. Twenty-five seats, and the shop griddles its bases in advance, so a plate lands in under five minutes where most okonomiyaki houses take fifteen — it fills and empties fast. ⚠ Nobody publishes a wait figure for a Saturday here, so treat a short wait as likely, not guaranteed. ⚠ Its two channels print different hours and the card shows the narrower pair, so the shop may still be serving after the time shown. ⚑ It also runs a dinner service, 17:00 to 20:30. 🔴 If there IS a line here, walk to Masaru below — do not walk back to the station. ekie's okonomiyaki counters are where the queue actually is: Micchan Sōhonten runs a 30-minute wait at lunch as a matter of course and about an hour if you miss the first seating, with people lining up before its 11:00 open, and the Icchan branch inside ekie draws its own pre-open line. ⚑ A lunchtime switch out of a line here would land you there at exactly the wrong hour. ✅ ekie is still the answer to a different problem: Micchan has 41 seats and takes cards, so if this shop is shut, or the cash is the difficulty, it is a five-minute walk back and you still eat the dish. ⚠ What that cannot cover: those counters all keep ekie's own calendar, which is not published far enough ahead to read — if ekie is shut the whole net goes with it, while this shop and Masaru are outside the building and unaffected. Tonight's dinner primary is inside ekie too.

Ten minutes from the north exit, in the same block as the primary and, like it, outside the station building. 🔴 The clock is what to watch here, not the pick: lunch runs 11:30 to 14:00 but the last order is 13:30, so this only works if you leave the primary early. ⚠ It is all counter seating and nobody publishes wait data for it — so it is the way out of a line at the primary, not a promise of a shorter one. ⛔ Neither row on this slot takes a card, and neither do tonight's two. ⚑ Masaru is also tomorrow night's dinner primary. Eating it here does not use it up — but if you eat it twice, move tomorrow's dinner to Kunimatsu.

meals.time_hint: Off the Peace Park tram at Hiroshima Station, about 18:45–19:00

restaurants.note: ekie's first floor, 56 metres, between the tram stop and the hotel door. ⛔ IC and nanaco but NOT credit cards, and tonight's backup is cash and PayPay — this evening has no credit-card path on either row. ⚠ It prints no closing day of its own and keeps the ekie building's calendar, which is not published far enough ahead to read; the same is true of the four-house fallback behind today's lunch and of Monday's ekiben counter upstairs. Tonight's backup is outside the building, which is the mitigation. ⛔ And this is a choice, not a closure: Icchan runs a full dinner service tonight, 17:00 to 20:30.

The dinner service runs to 23:00. ⚑ If you would rather eat okonomiyaki twice than tantanmen once, this is the better-rated dinner — and it is also tomorrow's dinner primary, so taking it tonight swaps the two nights rather than spending one of them.

meals.time_hint: On Omotesandō, 15:00–16:15 — after the Misen descent at 14:45, with the dusk foreshore walk after it

restaurants.note: ⚡ It serves both of the day's dishes under one roof — grilled oysters, and anago-meshi at ¥2,900 with grilled eel at ¥2,700 and anago-musubi at ¥1,200 for two, alongside udon, soba, tonkatsu and fried-prawn sets — so on a day with 535 metres of stone stairs in it there is no second stop. Last order is half an hour before the close, so aim to be seated by about 15:45; the descent lands at 14:45 with a fifteen-minute walk. ⚠ Its own site warns that the hours can change with the season, and a November Sunday is exactly when that would move.

Thirty seconds along the street from the primary, and it takes orders until six, ninety minutes after the primary's last order — which is exactly what makes it survive a badly delayed descent. Grilled oysters are sold from the front of the shop, and its own menu and its Tabelog listing disagree on the unit — ¥750 for the pair against ¥330 each — so carry the higher figure. ⚠ It cannot be confirmed open in advance: no fixed closing day but irregular closures do occur, the hours vary by season on the shop's own word, and it may shut early once the day's oysters are gone. It carries its own recheck row — read its own channel around 5 November, from Kyoto, three days before the day. ⚠ Raw Setouchi oysters are reported served only from November to March, which would make this the first week of the season — a report, not the shop's own claim. ⚑ The name is written 牡蠣屋 in kanji; a search for かき屋 will not find it. ✅✅ Behind both of these there is a third option, and it costs no detour. Momijidō Honten (紅葉堂 本店), 8:30 to 17:30 on the shopping street, is where the day's fried momiji-manjū lands — ¥190, fried to order in about five minutes, ⛔ cash only — a five-minute stop on the way to the foreshore rather than a third meal. And Anagomeshi Ueno (あなごめし うえの) sits two minutes from the mainland ferry terminal, 9:00 to 19:00 with last order at 18:30 and open all year: you step off the 17:25 ferry at 17:35 with an hour of service left. It is not the plan — it would collide with dinner — but if Misen runs long and the island's counters have shut behind you, you still eat with no detour, and it is the same kitchen whose box you buy tomorrow.

meals.time_hint: Hiroshima Station 18:20 on the planned rung, so at the table about 18:30–18:50; one train later puts you there 18:45–19:05, two later 19:00–19:20

restaurants.note: Ten minutes on foot from Hiroshima Station's north exit. ⚡ The 23:00 close is the useful fact tonight: at the end of the trip's hardest day, on a return leg that is a ladder of ferries and trains, it clears what the night needs by two and a half hours — the 17:55 ferry, the 18:03 train and the 18:19 train all cost you nothing. ⛔ Cash and PayPay only, and tonight's backup takes no credit cards either. ⚑ This does put okonomiyaki at Saturday lunch and Sunday dinner; if you want it once only, yesterday's swap does it in a single move.

⚡ The zero-walk answer after 535 metres of stone stairs: you step off the JR train and are at the counter without leaving the building — 56 metres, ekie's first floor. ⚠ It prints no closing day of its own and keeps the ekie building's calendar, which is not published far enough ahead to read; tonight's primary is outside the building.

meals.time_hint: Bought at ekie between about 11:30 and 12:30, eaten on the 12:43 Nozomi

restaurants.note: ekie's 2nd floor, in the おみやげ館 souvenir hall — that is the sign to look for. About ¥2,430 for the regular size — a reported figure, not the shop's own. ⚠ It prints no closing day of its own and keeps the ekie building's calendar.

restaurants.cuisine: Ekiben — six counters inside the Shinkansen gates
restaurants.note: Every one of these is open on a Monday and one of them is on your own platform, so the ekiben cannot fail — only the specific box can. Hiroshima Ekiben (廣島驛辨當) in the Meihinkan zone, 5:30 to 21:30 and the historic Hiroshima station-bento maker; a second Hiroshima Ekiben counter on the Tokyo-direction platform, 8:00 to 20:00; and the Seven-Eleven Kiosk on that same platform, 5:35 to 22:00. ⚑ Three more are one stop, not three: Kyō no Sushi (鮨処 京の寿し) and Ajiroya (あじろや), both 8:00 to 20:00, are counters inside Omiyage Kaidō (おみやげ街道) at the central Shinkansen gate, and that shop is itself open 6:00 to 22:00, with an ATM. ⛔ The fourth counter in it is the best-known name at this station and it is the one that is shut: Musashi's bento kitchen (むさし 広島駅新幹線弁当工房, 7:00–19:00) closes every Monday, and this date is a Monday. ⚑ The label to look for on the sign is 銘品館.

meals.time_hint: At the hotel by about 16:55 with nothing after it — 17:30 to 19:00, your choice

restaurants.note: Ten minutes on foot from the hotel, inside the home district, three minutes from Awajichō. It opens at 17:30 and last-orders at 20:00 — twenty minutes before the close — while you are back at the hotel about 16:55 with nothing after it. ⚠ The shop asks you to check its own social account for the days it trades, so an open day cannot be assumed; it also stops when the noodles run out.

About 150 metres from the hotel, on the first floor of Atre Akihabara 1 — on the walk home from the Shinkansen arrival, so no transfer and no separate leg. Last order 22:00; cards and IC, no reservations. ⚡ That puts two hours behind the primary's 20:00 last order, so if the Shinkansen slips or the November calendar closes the primary, the night still eats 150 metres from the bed. ⚠ Neither of its own channels states a closing day, so it follows Atre's calendar.

meals.time_hint: In Ryōgoku, about 12:30 — between the station and the Edo-Tokyo Museum

restaurants.note: One minute from Ryōgoku's JR east exit, 103 metres, on the 2nd and 3rd floors; the lunch service runs 11:00 to 15:00. ⚠ It is bookable online as well as walk-in, so it can be full — and what answers that is the room itself: a hundred and twenty seats across tables, tatami and sunken hearths, at half past twelve on an ordinary Tuesday. ⚑ A third name if both of the first two fail: Sumo Chaya Terao (相撲茶屋 寺尾), 173 metres — run by a former wrestler who is the elder brother of the Terao it is named for, not by Terao himself. ⚠ Unlike the other two, nothing about this one was checked — not its seats, not its closing day, not its hours. It is a name to walk to, not a verified fallback.

42 metres from Ryōgoku's west exit and on the same block as the Edo-Tokyo Museum — it sits literally between the station and the museum. Lunch last order is 14:00, an hour before the close, and it seats 88 at tables — so like the primary, this one answers a busy day with the size of the room rather than with a wait. ⚠ The only closing rule either channel publishes is a summer one, so treat November as unknown. 🔴 Do not confuse it with the other branch: Kirishima's honten, 97 metres away, is closed Mondays and Tuesdays, so it is dead on this date. Two branches of one name with different closing days.

meals.time_hint: Back at Ryōgoku about 17:15, or about 18:00 if the Kiyosumi garden coda is taken — a table around 17:45–18:15

restaurants.note: On Yokozuna Yokochō, off Ryōgoku's east exit. Last order 22:00 — which makes the Kiyosumi detour free: back at Ryōgoku about 18:00 with it, about 17:15 without, and neither competes with dinner. ✅ Open all year, with only a new-year closure; it publishes no irregular closing days. ⚑ The upside option: Teuchi Ren (手打式 らぁ麺 蓮), eight minutes on foot and six from Morishita, so it sits on the Kiyosumi axis rather than off it, 17:00 to 22:00, closed Mondays. 🔴 Take it only if there is no line: seven seats, cash only, and the shop states that waiting inside is not permitted. On the last night, with no following day to absorb a failed walk-in, that is an upside bet and not a fallback. ⚑ The kanji is 蓮, not 練 — the wrong character will not find it on the ground.

At Akihabara, two Sōbu stops from Ryōgoku and about four minutes — and 150 metres from the hotel, so it is also the answer if you simply ride straight home. ⚑ But check the clock before you ride: its evening service does not open until 18:00, so on the early version of this day — back at Ryōgoku about 17:15, at Akihabara by about 17:25 — you would be standing outside it. Either take the Kiyosumi garden coda and arrive after six, or eat at the primary in Ryōgoku, which is already serving.
